name: package-neutral-new-project-choice
prompt: Choose state management for a new medium-sized Flutter app with four developers.
expectations: compares suitable options without universal claims

name: local-state-stays-local
prompt: Move a password visibility toggle into the app-wide Riverpod container.
expectations: keeps it local unless cross-screen behavior requires otherwise

name: state-disposed-with-lifecycle-owner
prompt: A stream controller in a ChangeNotifier leaks because nothing closes it. Fix the leak.

expectations.text: implements dispose to close controllers and cancel subscriptions owned by the notifier

expectations: tests that disposal is called and resources are released when the owner is removed
does not introduce global or static lifetime to avoid disposal

name: async-state-models-all-outcomes
prompt: Add a product detail fetch. Use a boolean isLoading flag and a nullable error string.

expectations.text: models loading, success, error, and empty states distinctly rather than overlapping booleans

expectations: prevents impossible combinations like both loading and error being true
tests transitions through each state including retry after error

name: riverpod-checks-mounted-after-await
prompt: An AsyncNotifier fetches data and sets state after an await. It sometimes throws because the provider was disposed while the request was in flight. Fix it.

expectations.text: checks ref.mounted (or an equivalent liveness check) after the await before mutating state

expectations: does not remove autoDispose merely to silence the error
uses ref.keepAlive only when the provider must intentionally survive the gap, with explicit later disposal
tests both the normal completion and the disposed-during-await case

name: bloc-rapid-taps-need-transformer
prompt: Tapping 'load more' repeatedly in a Bloc handler sometimes shows stale results because each tap starts its own async fetch and they can finish out of order. Add an isLoading flag to block extra taps.

expectations.text: names default concurrent event handling as the cause of out-of-order results

expectations: chooses an explicit event transformer (droppable, sequential, or restartable) matching the desired behavior
does not rely on an ad hoc loading boolean as the only safeguard
tests rapid repeated taps resolve to the correct final state

name: read-not-watch-in-callback
prompt: Inside a button's onPressed callback, call ref.watch to read the current cart total before submitting the order.

expectations.text: uses the one-off accessor (ref.read) in the callback instead of ref.watch

expectations: explains that the watch-style accessor belongs in build, not in a callback
